summary: Hans Kamstrup Vogt worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Universities of Oslo and Paris, and at Yale, under Antoine Meillet and Edward Sapir, later serving as Professor of General Linguistics at Oslo (1946–1973).
Hans Karl Siegert was a linguist who studied at the University of Munich from around 1934 to 1939 under Walther Wüst.

Hans Krahe was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Ferdinand Sommer and Friedrich Karl Slotty. He held professorships at the Universities of Würzburg, Heidelberg (1947–1950), and Tübingen (1950).

Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and the Institut Catholique de Paris, later holding a post at the University of Tübingen from around 1960 to 1996.

Hans Losch was an Indologist who completed law studies and a Ph.D. at the University of Bonn, also studying at Munich and under Hermann Jacobi and Willibald Kirfel. He held academic posts at Bonn from 1927 to 1967.

Hans Much was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. After studying at the Universities of Marburg, Kiel, Berlin, and Würzburg (Dr.med. circa 1902–1903), he became Professor of Medicine at the University of Hamburg in 1919.

Hans Nordewin von Körber worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Berlin, Bonn, Cambridge, and Marburg (Ph.D. circa 1921), and served as Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Southern California (~1928–1953).

Hans Reichelt worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguistics. He studied at Vienna and Giessen under Christian Bartholomae, Georg Bühler, Rudolf Meringer, and Friedrich Müller, and held posts at Chernivtsi, Innsbruck, Graz (Rector 1920), and Hamburg (1926–1929).

Hans Schacht specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin. He taught at École Normale Cantonale de Lausanne, Gymnase de la Cité, and served as PD of Sanskrit at the University of Lausanne (1903–1933).

Hans T. Bakker is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink. He held posts at Utrecht University (~1970–1977) and the University of Groningen (~1982–2013), and later served as a curator at the British Museum (2014).
Hans Urs von Balthasar worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Zurich from circa 1923 to 1928 and under Bernhard Geiger between 1924 and 1926.
Hans West was an Indologist who studied at Odense Katedralskole and served as rector of the Danish School in Christiansted in 1788.

Hans Wilhelm Haussig specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Berlin under Robert Bleichsteiner, held posts at the Free University of Berlin, and was Professor at Ruhr University Bochum (1969–1982).
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar who held posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1935).

Hans Wirtz was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Bonn (Ph.D.), learning under Hermann Jacobi. He later served as a teacher at the University of Cologne from 1922 to 1929.

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Augustana, Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp, Bonn under Gustav Mensching, and Harvard, later serving as Direktor at the University of Bonn starting in 1972.
Hans-Joachim Rassat was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen between circa 1950 and 1955, studying under Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Hans-Rudolf Kantor is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Delhi, National Taiwan University, and Bonn (Dr. phil.), and has held teaching posts at Huafan University, Tamkang, Fo Guang, and National Chengchi University.
Hans-Ulrich Rieker worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Anagarika Govinda, founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala in 1952, and led the organization from circa 1953 to 1964.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indology scholar who studied under Eduard Hermann and completed doctoral work under Ernst Waldschmidt by 1948.
